description:
An audit of the test suite (14,765 tests, 68% coverage) found systematic
coverage theater - tests that inflate metrics without catching bugs.  The root
cause is per-file coverage enforcement (via `test_check_per_file_coverage.py`
and `test_check_module_coverage.py`) which incentivised an agent to produce 92
coverage-specific test files (`*coverage*.py`, `*wave_remaining*.py`) whose
tests mock everything and assert only that mocks behave as configured.

Key findings:
- 79 files named `*coverage*.py` + 13 `*wave_remaining*.py` (92 total)
- ~933 tests from these files, mostly mock-verify-mock tautologies
- 1,366 `isinstance()` assertions across 295 files (many trivial)
- Pattern: mock class -> call method -> assert mock returned what you told it to
- Pattern: instantiate dataclass -> assert attributes equal constructor args
- Pattern: 300-line fake framework (test_unified_frame_coverage.py) that
  diverges from real API silently
- Estimated meaningful coverage: 30-40% (vs reported 68%)

This TODO remediates in phases: first remove perverse incentives, then triage
the 92 files, then write replacement tests for critical paths.

anti_patterns.instead: assert on computed values and behavior instead
anti_patterns.why: these are precisely the hollow assertions being removed

anti_patterns.instead: delete and replace with real tests
anti_patterns.why: false confidence from passing hollow tests is worse than no test at all
this recreates the perverse incentive that caused the theater

anti_patterns.dont: write replacement tests that mock the database connection
anti_patterns.why: mock connections are the root cause of the current theater
